HERF STREET 22

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
If someone acted, two year old Chevonne Rusch may still have been alive.

Unique Selling Point:
This is the story of Chevonne Rusch in her last days before she was brutally murdered by her mother's boyfriend while her mother was watching. What happens when a mother and family fails a child, who becomes responsible?

Summary:
Verdict has finally been made in the Chevonne Rusch trial. Her mother together with her former boyfriend Stephan van Niekerk are guilty of murder. The mother, Rochelle Botha has further been found guilty on cases of severe child neglect, abuse, and trafficking. Sentencing will be heard on 2 February.
It was a death that sparked outrage in May 2022, when pictures of a little blonde girl were shared on social media. Now, two years later, the court had found that her own mother is responsible for her death and faces two life sentences. But this is not why we need to tell the story. If the authorities reacted to calls from the community and friends, Chevonne, her sister and small brother, may have been given a chance on a normal life. Instead, they have been abused for years.
Friends and family made various attempts to the police and social services for help after Stephan cut Chevonne’s little brother with an angle grinder. All these attempts were in vain.
Chevonne’s story has been heard by the courts and hers becomes the voice of so many oth er vulnerable children who will never be heard. Children who can be saved if the department of social development was more proactive, especially in Gauteng. Now, further insult to injury will occur given the province’s decision taken by the premier to cut all funding to private NGO’s, leaving cases like Chevonne’s solely in the hands of the state.


Further information:
PART 1: WHO WAS CHEVONNE AND WHAT HAPPENED AT HERF STREET 25 ON 11 MAY 2022?
- First she was taken to the primrose clinic and died a few minutes after her arrival.
- Then her mother’s boyfriend, Stefan van Niekerk, is arrested.
- Then Chevonne’s mother, Rochelle Botha, disappears for six weeks while she lies in a mortuary. A funeral cannot be arranged because there is no birth certificate. Rochelle allegedly sold the clinic card when the child was born and never registered her.
- Six weeks later, a funeral is held at the chapel next to the mortuary. Rochelle arrives at the funeral and carries the coffin into the chapel together with the baby’s father, Bradly to the tune of Dance Monkey. Rochelle does not sit inside the church, instead she sits on the staircase outside, head between her legs, crying. The priests talks gives the congregation a hard talk about drugs and child abuse and blames the family for putting their own drug abuse interest before that of a small child.
- Then Rochelle is arrested. Protests starts outside courts- resulting in both Stefan and Rochelle abandoning their bail application. They were in custory for a year before the trail started in October 2023.
- Both are convicted of murder.

PART 2: COULD CHEVONNE HAVE BEEN SAVED? IF A CHILD’S HOME CIRCUMSTANCES ARE TOO DANGEROUS FOR HIM TO LIVE IN, WHAT THEN, DOES HE BECOME THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE STATE? AND WHAT IF THE STATE DOES NOT DO ITS JOB?

- Long before Chevonne’s murder, friends and family alerted the police about the abuse of Chevonne’s brother. Stefan had cut the child with a grinder to the head. Kayla alerted the authorities but was turned away. She says that Rochelle was under Stefan’s influence. That Stefan drugged Rochelle and then abused the children. Question is, did Rochelle not just drug herself? We know that she rented her body out to buy drugs, but did she also rent out her children? Did Stefan? If children are living in these circumstances, what then? What is the role of the community and the state?
- If cases are reported, where does bureaucracy end and help begin? If family and friends who know no better, contact the first available number they think can assist, and are shown away, who’s responsibility does it become to ‘save the children’ from their circumstances. So if you call the welfare services, and they tell you that the area you refer to is not under their jurisdiction, can they then just turn a blind eye, hoping that the person who contacted them will contact the right authority?
- A week before her death, Chanelle Brummer took Chevonne in. She made sure that the child was dressed and gave her food. But she is not the legal guardian. She contacted ChildLine and took the child back to where she found her, hoping someone will intervene, but no one did. Who’s responsibility was Chevonne? Did every single person in her life fail her?

PART 3 : THE GAPS IN THE SOCIAL WELFARE SYSTEM AND BETWEEN THE POLICE AND JUSTICE
- Even after she was murdered and no one saved her, she was further failed by the police. The police decided it was a drowning and did not open a full murder investigation. They never went to the house to do the forensic investigation and appointed someone inadequate to do the investigation. This resulted in civil society, taking over the work of the police. If it wasn’t for civil society, who knows what affidavits would have been taken and if the court would finally have anyting to work with?

First the system that is supposed to save her life, fails her. Then Chevonne is further failed by the state that could not even resolve her murder. Yes her mother’s boyfriend is behind bars and so is her mother. But what about the other horrible things that happened to her and her siblings in their short lives? Chevonne was raped, but there is no investigation into this and those who continuously raped her during her two years on this earth, are free to live their lives.

Unique Selling Point: This is the story of Chevonne Rusch in her last days before she was brutally murdered by her mother's boyfriend while her mother was watching. What happens when a mother and family fails a child, who becomes responsible? Summary: Verdict has finally been made in the Chevonne Rusch trial. Her mother together with her former boyfriend Stephan van Niekerk are guilty of murder. The mother, Rochelle Botha has further been found guilty on cases of severe child neglect, abuse, and trafficking. Sentencing will be heard on 2 February. It was a death that sparked outrage in May 2022, when pictures of a little blonde girl were shared on social media. Now, two years later, the court had found that her own mother is responsible for her death and faces two life sentences. But this is not why we need to tell the story. If the authorities reacted to calls from the community and friends, Chevonne, her sister and small brother, may have been given a chance on a normal life. Instead, they have been abused for years. Friends and family made various attempts to the police and social services for help after Stephan cut Chevonne’s little brother with an angle grinder. All these attempts were in vain. Chevonne’s story has been heard by the courts and hers becomes the voice of so many oth er vulnerable children who will never be heard. Children who can be saved if the department of social development was more proactive, especially in Gauteng. Now, further insult to injury will occur given the province’s decision taken by the premier to cut all funding to private NGO’s, leaving cases like Chevonne’s solely in the hands of the state. Further information: PART 1: WHO WAS CHEVONNE AND WHAT HAPPENED AT HERF STREET 25 ON 11 MAY 2022? - First she was taken to the primrose clinic and died a few minutes after her arrival. - Then her mother’s boyfriend, Stefan van Niekerk, is arrested. - Then Chevonne’s mother, Rochelle Botha, disappears for six weeks while she lies in a mortuary. A funeral cannot be arranged because there is no birth certificate. Rochelle allegedly sold the clinic card when the child was born and never registered her. - Six weeks later, a funeral is held at the chapel next to the mortuary. Rochelle arrives at the funeral and carries the coffin into the chapel together with the baby’s father, Bradly to the tune of Dance Monkey. Rochelle does not sit inside the church, instead she sits on the staircase outside, head between her legs, crying. The priests talks gives the congregation a hard talk about drugs and child abuse and blames the family for putting their own drug abuse interest before that of a small child. - Then Rochelle is arrested. Protests starts outside courts- resulting in both Stefan and Rochelle abandoning their bail application. They were in custory for a year before the trail started in October 2023. - Both are convicted of murder. PART 2: COULD CHEVONNE HAVE BEEN SAVED? IF A CHILD’S HOME CIRCUMSTANCES ARE TOO DANGEROUS FOR HIM TO LIVE IN, WHAT THEN, DOES HE BECOME THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE STATE? AND WHAT IF THE STATE DOES NOT DO ITS JOB? - Long before Chevonne’s murder, friends and family alerted the police about the abuse of Chevonne’s brother. Stefan had cut the child with a grinder to the head. Kayla alerted the authorities but was turned away. She says that Rochelle was under Stefan’s influence. That Stefan drugged Rochelle and then abused the children. Question is, did Rochelle not just drug herself? We know that she rented her body out to buy drugs, but did she also rent out her children? Did Stefan? If children are living in these circumstances, what then? What is the role of the community and the state? - If cases are reported, where does bureaucracy end and help begin? If family and friends who know no better, contact the first available number they think can assist, and are shown away, who’s responsibility does it become to ‘save the children’ from their circumstances. So if you call the welfare services, and they tell you that the area you refer to is not under their jurisdiction, can they then just turn a blind eye, hoping that the person who contacted them will contact the right authority? - A week before her death, Chanelle Brummer took Chevonne in. She made sure that the child was dressed and gave her food. But she is not the legal guardian. She contacted ChildLine and took the child back to where she found her, hoping someone will intervene, but no one did. Who’s responsibility was Chevonne? Did every single person in her life fail her? PART 3 : THE GAPS IN THE SOCIAL WELFARE SYSTEM AND BETWEEN THE POLICE AND JUSTICE - Even after she was murdered and no one saved her, she was further failed by the police. The police decided it was a drowning and did not open a full murder investigation. They never went to the house to do the forensic investigation and appointed someone inadequate to do the investigation. This resulted in civil society, taking over the work of the police. If it wasn’t for civil society, who knows what affidavits would have been taken and if the court would finally have anyting to work with? First the system that is supposed to save her life, fails her. Then Chevonne is further failed by the state that could not even resolve her murder. Yes her mother’s boyfriend is behind bars and so is her mother. But what about the other horrible things that happened to her and her siblings in their short lives? Chevonne was raped, but there is no investigation into this and those who continuously raped her during her two years on this earth, are free to live their lives. FADE OUT PART 1 VO PLEASE PUT LOCATION STRAP IN CORNER RIGHT: GERMISTON, GAUTENG Deserted, damaged, neglected…this house resembles the story of its last occupants. No traces of a family that was once happy here – only the echoes of two-year old’s cries…fighting for her life against an adult man, with her mother nearby. While sentencing is pending in the murder trial of Chevonne Avril Rusch, the events that unfolded here in May 2022 remain veiled in mystery. LINK SOURCE: DAY 2 C8562 “It is really eerie being at this property two years after Chevonne’s murder and we know that critical events happened behind this window in the bathroom, but what’s more, its understood that several incidents of severe child abuse happened on this property and have never come to light” PAUSE CHANGE GEAR VO Rochelle Botha and Bradleigh Rusch had three children - Chevonne was the youngest. SUPER@ KIRSTI ANN HOSSEN “KAYLA: SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:38:28:08 “Stefan isolated Rochelle from her family” VO Rochelle’s lifelong friend, Kayla Hossen, discovered that Stefan was abusive when she saw marks on Chevonne’s four-year old brother’s body. SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:28:22:38 “Every time there was a mark on Chevonne’s brother’s body, Stefan always had the excuse why that mark was there” VO Kayla - and Rochelle's family - did confront Stefan. He evaded them. Until his abuse of the four-year-old little boy escalated to extreme brutality. SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:40:49:28 “His backside was black, purple, blue horrifically. Dit het gelyk soos, if you touch it, it would pop”. SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:44:39:16 I mean, they cut him on the head with a fucking angle grinder. VO To save Rochelle’s son’s life, Kayla reached out to the authorities. PHOTOS OF JAYDEN’S BLUE BUM SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: DAY 2 FX3_9373 02:20:42:25 “I went to the child welfare in Edenvale and they turned me away. They said that due to jurisdictional laws there was nothing they could do. I then went to Childline Gauteng, which is the whole of Gauteng. They directed me to 10111 which directed me to the police and I couldn’t get through; the land line was just ringing. VO I was saying to God, please God, just one person, one person to hear our cry for help” VO Finally, a police officer went to the house, but stayed outside the gates. SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:26:11:33 “He said to me I know the place now, but there is a procedure to follow, that just hit me like. It was like me bashing into the wall” SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:25:53:08 “I just want this child removed with immediate effect. Like right now, break through the gates and grab this child”. VO Undeterred, Stefan turned on Chevonne too. She suffered violent abuse and severe neglect. At the beginning of May, without any explanation, she was dropped off at Stefan’s brother house nearby. CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 C8472 15:46:52:28 “Sy was in ‘n walglike toestand toe ek haar ontmoet het”. SUBS: She was in a terrible state when I met her” VO When Chanelle Brummer, a beauty therapist from Boksburg, visited the brother’s house, she met Chevonne for the first time and she could see something was very wrong. ADD ERIN’S QUESTION JUST TO GIVE HER PRESENCE. CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 15:50:35:19 “Chevonne was in pyn gewees. CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 C8472 15:49:01:39 Dit is toe die dag wat ek toe besluit het ek gaan die kind huistoe neem. CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 15:53:18:10 “Sy het net geskree, die enigste tyd wat sy opgehou skree het was voor sy gaan slaap het, toe ek haar rustig gekry het, selfs toe ek haar gebad het, sy het vreeslik geskree. SUBS: She was just screaming. The only time she stopped screaming was when she went to bed. Even when I bathed her, she was screaming. In the morning when she woke up, I gave her yoghurt VO Taking photos of Chevonne’s injuries, Chanelle reached out to Childline. CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 15:54:14:03 ek het vir hulle adresse gestuur en ek het vir hulle gevra om net te gaan kyk en ek het genoem dat hulle gou moet maak want daar is ander kinders ook wat ek bewus van is”. SUBS: I googles child abuse and came across Child Line SA. I emailed the photos to them and I gave them addresses. I asked them to investigate and told them to hurry, that there were other children. VO Chanelle returned Chevonne to Stefan's family, expecting her evidence to mobilise the authorities. All she received was an automated email from Childline redirecting her to the police and welfare. All the while, Chevonne’s abuse worsened. Four days later, she was killed. PAUSE VO CHANELLE BRUMMER TRANSCRIPTIONS SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 15:56:26:44 As iemand uitgegaan het, as iemand iets gedoen het, dan was sy hier vandag.” SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 02:55:24:09 “A child is dead today because they did not act” VO Are bureaucratic hurdles preventing authorities from saving children in real danger? PAUSE Putting ourselves in the shoes of an ordinary person, we search online for the nearest police station to our filming location. POLICE UNDERCOVER; ERIN ;TRANSCRIPTIONS SOURCE: DAY 2 C8512 16:32:49:22 ERIN: What can I do if I know that my neighbour is beating their child? COP: You must go to the social workers ERIN: Social workers? ERIN: But if it is happening at the moment? Like I know today, that child is beaten and getting black and blue. COP: Listen, I don’t know whether you don’t hear me, or what. VO Child welfare expert Dr. Joan Van Niekerk says the police should intervene, regardless of jurisdiction. SUPER@ JOAN VAN NIEKERK: SOCIAL WORK EXPERT SOURCE: ZOOM INTERVIEW 2 00:15:44:07 “The police instructions on sexual offences against children, are you may not turn anybody, who reports a case of child abuse, sexual abuse in particular, away, it happens all the time because they don’t know what to do”. VO It seems that’s exactly what happened in Chevonne’s case. SUPER@ JOAN VAN NIEKERK: SOCIAL WORK EXPERT SOURCE: ZOOM INTERVIEW 2 00:15:01:12 Our police training is now cut down to a year. What a police person can learn in that year in terms of their responsibilities how they manage allegations of drug trafficking or situations of domestic violence or drug abuse, they cannot learn all of that in a year and yet these are the people who sit at the front desk of our police service stations”. SOURCE: DAY 2 C8512 16:34:09:15 “So how do I get hold of the social worker? Do you have a number for me or a name of someone? COP: No, no. you go there by SASSA SUPER@ JOAN VAN NIEKERK: SOCIAL WORK EXPERT SOURCE: ZOOM INTERVIEW 2 00:10:12:13 “SASSA office is not involved in child protection matters. They deal with grants. To refer a child protection issue to them is ridiculous”. VO Following the police’s directions, we proceed to SASSA’s office. VOICE: “Regarding what?” ERIN: If I have a case of child abuse that I need to report? VOICE: Its not the second floor?” ERIN: I don’t know, they said third floor. VO We’re sent from pillar to post in this building - no urgency to help us - mirroring the barriers in reporting Chevonne’s case. 16:48:55:19 “So now I must go downstairs? Is it second floor not third floor?” 16:49:13:30 ERIN: Hi, how are you? VOICE: good ERIN: Are you a social worker? VOICE: Yes ERIN: Oh good, ok. If I need to report a case of child abuse… VOICE: oh first floor. LINK SOURCE: DAY 2 FX3_9369 02:17:00:47 “If there is one thing this experience has taught me, is that you’re pretty much on your own when it comes to report child abuse. And if you don’t have the resources, whether that is energy, transport or airtime, the case can simply fall through the cracks and another child could end up dead” VO Even after death, the system continued to fail Chevonne. There were four people inside the house when she was killed: Stefan, Rochelle and two of Stefan’s friends. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 00:32:49:17 “There were four people in a house where a little girl died, I would have like to get them all in the dock to see them explain to the court what happened in that house that night, but it didn’t happen” VO Former cop Annari Du Plessis, now heading the Purple Foundation for abused children, played a pivotal role in the investigation. In her view the police procrastinated. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 00:21:47:02 “And in two days, throughout two days, there were ball playing on who should take this case. And most of the WhatsApp screenshots in this matter was in Afrikaans And then eventually the case was handed to an IO, a young police constable, female who could not speak one word of Afrikaans. VO After hours of abuse, Chevonne had lost consciousness. Stefan, and one of his two friends in the house, took the child to the Wannenberg clinic on the East Rand. Stefan told staff that Chevonne had drowned. LINK SOURCE: DAY 1 C8458 “If it weren’t for staff at this clinic, there might not even have been a murder case. They could tell from Chevonne’s multiple and severe injuries that something terrible had been done to her”. VO The clinic called the police and Stefan was arrested - but on an outstanding warrant for another crime. It’s only when public pressure mounted that a murder docket was opened for Chevonne. Annari literally moved into the police station to asist the investigation. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 00:22:20:33 “On the second day, I brought my printer, I called the Afrikaanssprekende witnesses to come and meet at the police station, their statements were taken. We were really actively involved in getting the job done”. VO Meanwhile, Kayla found Stefan’s two friends still residing in the house, days after the murder. SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 03:04:22:30 The police never treated this like a crime scene. VO Police detectives visited the crime scene after eight days - for the first time. They didn't even take photos - Annari took some evidence on her phone. SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 00:28:08:08 “I saw a pillow and it was clear for me, there were blood on the pillow. I saw spats against the wall, and I was like, Colonel, we need to get the forensics team here” ERIN: FORENSICS weren’t with you? ANNARI: No! he was saying to me, Annari no I am not gonna get them to come here because there were other people, the scene is old, it’s been contaminated already. I understood that but for me, the spats on the wall, the pillow, let’s just take a chance, let’s just see what we can get here. let’s do the work and I could see that he didn’t want to”. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 01:12:16:08 “If the forensics were there I can guarantee you now, there would have been four suspects, four guilty findings, four sentences” VO Initially, only Stefan was in custody. Chevonne's body lay in the mortuary for nearly a month. Annari showed us evidence that Rochelle had sold Chevonne’s clinic card after her birth… the child was never properly registered. When a funeral was finally held for her in the mortuary's chapel, her mother sat on the stairs outside. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 00:53:49:49 She was sitting with me outside, she didn’t want to go inside and at that stage it was strange for me because I was sitting with a woman that I know was lying. I couldn’t say that she hurt her child, but I know she was there and that she did very little to protect her daughter”. VO The experts say if a mother witnessed such torture and did nothing, she is viewed as a perpetrator. VO This is a voice recording of Rochelle, the night after the murder. UPSOUND SOURCE: VOICENOTE 2 7:38 Sy het geskree, mommy help me, mommy please. VOICENOTE 3 6:00 Dan hoor ek Gwa Gwa gwa as ek ingaan dan skree ek, stefan hou nou op. Ek was ignore gewees. Wat moet ek vir die mense se as die mense vra? SUBS: I heard gwa gwa gwa and yelled, Stefan stop it! I was ignored. What must I say if people ask? VO Police finally arrested Rochelle after three months. The two friends were only called as witnesses, as police never linked them to any of the crimes SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 38:44:32 “They testified, that sound makes me, I want to vomit, when the judge read, the witnesses testified that they heard a glug glug sound from the bathroom and I was thinking, you did nothing? You could’ve saved her, but you did nothing” VO Rochelle and Stefan were found guilty on charges of murder and rape. PAUSE Chevonne’s story echoes that of countless children - failed by a system that was meant to protect them. Every adult bears a duty to report child abuse, but the question remains: to whom? SUPER@ CHANELLE BRUMMER SOURCE: DAG 2 C8486 16:21:07:13 “Die laaste week van haar lewe het sy ‘n bad gehad, sy het kossies gehad, sy was warm, sy het ‘n kombersie gehad, ek het haar die heeltyd vasgehou”. SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 01:00:54:21 “Inevitably, there will be another body bag wit a child severely and brutally killed. Staff can immediately tell from her multiple and severe injuries; someone has done something terrible.. But who is responsible? SOURCE: DAY 1 FX3_9332 SUPER@ANNARI DU PLESSIS: PURPLE FOUNDATION 39:07:27 “We still don’t know completely what happened to little Chevonne” SUPER@ KIRSTY-ANN HOSSEN SOURCE: FX3_9373 03:04:22:30 “Rochelle wasn’t there when that baby was killed. I am so certain of what I am saying. Rochelle is not guilty. I believe the wrong people are in jail. The police never treated this like a crime scene”. She covered in a blanket, like I looked at her for a very long time. and I was like, how the fuck did anyone let this happen?” VO This is the story of two year old Chevonne Rusch, abused, and battered to death. Protests starts outside courts- resulting in both Stefan and Rochelle abandoning their bail application. They were in custory for a year before the trail started in October 2023. - Both are convicted of murder. PART 2: COULD CHEVONNE HAVE BEEN SAVED? IF A CHILD’S HOME CIRCUMSTANCES ARE TOO DANGEROUS FOR HIM TO LIVE IN, WHAT THEN, DOES HE BECOME THE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE STATE? AND WHAT IF THE STATE DOES NOT DO ITS JOB? - Long before Chevonne’s murder, friends and family alerted the police about the abuse of Chevonne’s brother. Stefan had cut the child with a grinder to the head. Kayla alerted the authorities but was turned away. She says that Rochelle was under Stefan’s influence. That Stefan drugged Rochelle and then abused the children. Question is, did Rochelle not just drug herself? We know that she rented her body out to buy drugs, but did she also rent out her children? Did Stefan? If children are living in these circumstances, what then? What is the role of the community and the state? - If cases are reported, where does bureaucracy end and help begin? If family and friends who know no better, contact the first available number they think can assist, and are shown away, who’s responsibility does it become to ‘save the children’ from their circumstances. So if you call the welfare services, and they tell you that the area you refer to is not under their jurisdiction, can they then just turn a blind eye, hoping that the person who contacted them will contact the right authority? - A week before her death, Chanelle Brummer took Chevonne in. She made sure that the child was dressed and gave her food. But she is not the legal guardian. She contacted ChildLine and took the child back to where she found her, hoping someone will intervene, but no one did. Who’s responsibility was Chevonne? Did every single person in her life fail her? PART 3 : THE GAPS IN THE SOCIAL WELFARE SYSTEM AND BETWEEN THE POLICE AND JUSTICE - Even after she was murdered and no one saved her, she was further failed by the police. The police decided it was a drowning and did not open a full murder investigation. They never went to the house to do the forensic investigation and appointed someone inadequate to do the investigation. This resulted in civil society, taking over the work of the police. If it wasn’t for civil society, who knows what affidavits would have been taken and if the court would finally have anyting to work with? First the system that is supposed to save her life, fails her. Then Chevonne is further failed by the state that could not even resolve her murder. Yes her mother’s boyfriend is behind bars and so is her mother. But what about the other horrible things that happened to her and her siblings in their short lives? Chevonne was raped, but there is no investigation into this and those who continuously raped her during her two years on this earth, are free to live their lives.
